Hi there — happy to explain.

On Novig, both order types are ways to enter a trade on a contract, but they differ in how the price is set:

• Limit order: You choose the maximum price you’ll pay (if buying) or the minimum price you’ll accept (if selling). Your order will only fill at your limit price or better. If there isn’t enough liquidity at that price, it may fill partially or remain open until someone matches it (or until you cancel it).

• Market order: You’re prioritizing getting filled quickly. The order will match immediately against the best available prices in the order book at that moment, which means the final average fill price can vary depending on available liquidity (and can be worse than you expect in a thin market).

When to use each:
• Use a limit order when price matters to you and you’re okay waiting for a match.
• Use a market order when speed matters more than price certainty (especially if the market is liquid).

If you tell us the market you’re looking at and whether you’re trying to buy or sell, we can also point out where to view current bid/ask prices so you can choose an order type confidently.

Novig Support

Hi there — happy to explain how matching works on Novig.

In general, orders are matched based on the best available price first, and when multiple orders are at the same price, the earliest order in the queue is filled first (often called price-time priority).

If two orders are placed at the exact same limit price “at the same time,” the system still has to sequence them (down to milliseconds). The order that is received/accepted by our matching engine first will be ahead in the queue at that price level.

A couple quick related details:
- A limit order can fill immediately (partially or fully) if there’s an opposing order available at your price or better; any unfilled remainder stays on the book at your limit price.
- If you share the market you’re looking at (and whether you’re placing bids/asks or buying/selling YES/NO), we can walk through a concrete example with numbers.
